intuition.title: Combustion and crystallization are distinct stages
intuition.text: The 650 °C, 30 min air treatment produces a gray, amorphous combustion body. The brief 1150 °C, 90 s air treatment produces the yellow crystalline YAG:Ce body. The reported 18 nm Scherrer domain size belongs to the final product, not the amorphous intermediate. Above 1150 °C or at longer times the authors report larger grains and more sintering; below 1000 °C they report amorphous white, nonluminescent samples. No discrete comparison times or full schedules are given.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Synthesis and thermal comparison

intuition.title: Clusters, crystallites and surface-linked molecules
intuition.text: Grinding and sonic-bath treatment yield 100–1000 nm clusters made from an interconnected network of approximately 20 nm nanocrystals by TEM/HRTEM. These scales are distinct from the 18 nm XRD coherent-domain estimate. Glycine is proposed to bridge the YAG:Ce surface and TRITC through its carboxylic and primary-amine groups; this is not an experimentally determined surface molecular structure.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Figure 2 and conjugation discussion

intuition.title: Energy transfer is inferred from spectra and decay
intuition.text: At 440 nm excitation, TRITC absorbs weakly but conjugate emission is dominated by the dye. The conjugate also shows faster Ce emission decay monitored at 520 nm. The authors infer predominantly nonradiative dipole–dipole energy transfer and estimate an average rate of approximately 10^8–10^9 s−1; donor–acceptor distances and size polydispersity prevent a precise quantitative rate distribution. The 60 ns host time is defined at intensity 1/e, rather than a fitted universal lifetime.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figures 3–4 and energy-transfer discussion

intuition.title: The shell is an explanatory distance model
intuition.text: The source estimates a critical transfer distance of approximately 7 nm using Förster–Dexter theory. A modeled outer 5 nm shell of an 18 nm YAG:Ce crystal places more than 90% of Ce ions within transfer distance of the surface. This is a statistical energy-transfer picture, not a measured core–shell particle or compositional map.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Equation and following paragraph

intuition.title: Photobleaching probes the dye contribution
intuition.text: After 65 h irradiation at 300 nm from a 450 W xenon lamp, the conjugate becomes slightly yellow and the dye spectral contribution falls. Bleaching is incomplete; the authors suggest strong scattering limits light penetration. The remaining fast decay has a smaller contribution. No new numerical post-bleach lifetime or particle structure is reported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4, Figure 5 and photobleaching discussion

intuition.title: Alternative fuels and a negative dye control
intuition.text: Urea and citric acid are separate fuel alternatives reported to yield 23 nm crystals with lower quantum yield and more sintering. Their complete recipes are not supplied. A separate glycine/Rhodamine B treatment does not produce a dye–nanocrystal conjugate; its amounts and workup are not independently specified and are not filled from the TRITC recipe.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
